one_sentence_story: Inspired by a lemon-juice bank heist, Justin Kruger and David Dunning showed in 1999 that lacking a skill also blinds you to spotting your own mistakes (12th percentile thinking they're 62nd) — while debunking the fake internet 'Mount Stupid' graph and proving 10 minutes of real training cures the blind spot.
so_what_for_you: Welcome the moment a new skill suddenly makes you feel humble — that dip means you finally know enough to spot errors; and always use external checklists or mentors in unfamiliar territory.

jargon_map.plain: experts assuming everyone else found the test easy too, making them underestimate their relative rank
